scope: Native existing single-atom SELECT compilation and paged aggregates; does not measure compound throughput, file-query/logical workloads, source I/O, authority, transport, or installed recovery.
method: Seven alternating paired process samples with one warm-up per binary, same ReleaseSafe driver and iteration/row counts; shared host with concurrent qualification. Raw samples and hashes below. No deadlines or performance budgets were changed.
decisions: Retain bounded compact AST storage and full eager Boolean semantics; never reserve a maximum literal buffer for each instruction.
Retain internal AST borrowing during native compile: SELECT medians improve 7–10% against initial compound parser.
Retain parseInto and direct predicate output: SELECT medians improve another 15–33% against internal borrowing alone.
Reject and revert the special single-atom parser path: predicate cases improve about 3%, but no-WHERE cases regress 4.5–5.2%; no consistent overall improvement justifies the extra path.

Final comparison against saved-program control still shows SELECT compile medians 18.6–33.5% higher (about 0.17–0.48 microseconds). Existing aggregate medians are 2.3–2.8% lower; this is not a general performance pass.
